title: DevOps Engineering
subtitle: Professional Training Curriculum
audience_line: Developers, system administrators and IT engineers moving into DevOps roles
overview: This programme takes participants from a shared Git repository to a monitored application running in production, using the tools teams actually run today. It follows the path of a single change: version control and collaboration, continuous integration and delivery with Jenkins and GitHub Actions, code quality and artifact management, infrastructure provisioned with Terraform and configured with Ansible, then metrics and alerts with Prometheus and Grafana. Every chapter is hands-on, the same application is carried through all phases, and the programme ends with a final project that assembles the whole delivery chain.

facts.label: Audience
facts.value: Developers, system administrators and IT engineers moving into DevOps roles

facts.label: Prerequisites
facts.value: Linux command line and Bash (course: Linux & Bash Scripting); Docker and Kubernetes basics (course: Docker & Kubernetes)

facts.label: Duration
facts.value: 81 h: 72 h of chapters + 9 h buffer, in 27 sessions of 3 h

facts.label: Format
facts.value: Short lectures followed by guided labs; one application carried through every phase

facts.label: Assessment
facts.value: Lab completion per phase and a final project presented to the group

facts.label: Outcome
facts.value: Participants can build, secure the quality of, deploy and monitor an application through a complete automated pipeline

phases.name: DevOps Culture & Collaboration
phases.focus: DevOps principles, Git and team workflows
phases.intro: DevOps starts with how a team works, then with how it shares code. This phase sets the vocabulary and metrics used for the rest of the programme, and makes every participant fluent with Git and pull-request based collaboration.

chapters.title: DevOps Culture
chapters.content: CALMS, the four DORA metrics, Agile and Kanban, value streams, where automation pays off

chapters.title: Git Internals
chapters.content: Why version control, distributed vs centralised, blobs, trees, commits and tags, the .git directory

chapters.title: Core Git Workflow
chapters.content: init, clone, add, commit, status, log, diff, .gitignore, commit message conventions, atomic commits

chapters.title: Branching & Merging
chapters.content: Branch model, fast-forward and three-way merges, rebase, cherry-pick, conflict resolution

chapters.title: Remote Repositories & GitHub
chapters.content: fetch, pull, push, SSH vs HTTPS authentication, forks, origin and upstream, pull requests

chapters.title: Team Workflow
chapters.content: GitFlow vs trunk-based development, code review, branch protection rules, release tags, semantic versioning

phases.name: Continuous Integration & Delivery
phases.intro: Participants build the same pipeline twice: on a self-hosted Jenkins server, as most companies run on premises, and on GitHub Actions, as most cloud-native teams do. Code quality gates and artifact management are added so that only tested, versioned builds move forward.

chapters.title: Jenkins Foundations
chapters.content: Installation, plugins, security settings, controller and agent architecture, job types

chapters.title: Jenkins Pipelines
chapters.content: Declarative pipelines, stages and steps, post actions, parameters, environment variables

chapters.title: Triggers & Credentials
chapters.content: Webhooks, SCM polling, scheduled builds, credential types and secure use in pipelines

chapters.title: Scaling Jenkins
chapters.content: Distributed agents, parallel stages, shared libraries for reusable pipeline code

chapters.title: Deploying from Jenkins
chapters.content: Build and push container images, deploy to Kubernetes, archive artifacts

chapters.title: GitHub Actions
chapters.content: Workflows, events, jobs and steps, hosted and self-hosted runners, matrix builds, caching

chapters.title: Secure Delivery with Actions
chapters.content: Secrets, environments and approvals, OIDC federation to the cloud, deployment workflows

chapters.title: Code Quality with SonarQube
chapters.content: Static analysis, coverage reports, quality profiles, quality gates that block a pipeline

chapters.title: Artifact Management with Nexus
chapters.content: Hosted, proxy and group repositories, versioning, retention policies, publishing from the pipeline

phases.name: Infrastructure as Code
phases.intro: Servers and cloud resources are described in code, reviewed like code and applied by the pipeline. Ansible configures machines; Terraform creates the infrastructure they run on. Each tool ends with a small project that the final project reuses.

chapters.title: IaC & Ansible Basics
chapters.content: Declarative vs imperative, configuration drift, Ansible architecture, static inventory, ad hoc commands

chapters.title: Playbooks
chapters.content: YAML, plays and tasks, core modules, handlers, conditionals, idempotency

chapters.title: Variables, Templates & Vault
chapters.content: group_vars and host_vars, Jinja2 templates and filters, Ansible Vault for secrets

chapters.title: Roles
chapters.content: Role structure, defaults, dependencies, Ansible Galaxy, designing reusable roles

chapters.title: Ansible Project
chapters.content: Configure a multi-server web stack: web server, application, database, TLS

chapters.title: Terraform Foundations
chapters.content: Providers, HCL syntax, resources, data sources, dependency graph, plan and apply

chapters.title: Terraform State & Variables
chapters.content: Variables and validation, outputs, state, remote backends and state locking

chapters.title: Modules & Environments
chapters.content: Writing and versioning modules, workspaces, import of existing resources, code organisation

chapters.title: Terraform Project
chapters.content: Provision the cloud environment (network, compute, database) for the course application

phases.name: Observability
phases.focus: Prometheus metrics and alerts, Grafana dashboards
phases.intro: A delivery chain is only finished when the team can see what runs in production. Participants instrument the course application, write the queries behind useful dashboards and turn them into alerts.

chapters.title: Prometheus
chapters.content: Metrics model, exporters, service discovery, PromQL, recording and alerting rules

chapters.title: Grafana
chapters.content: Data sources, dashboards, alerting and notification channels, service level objectives

phases.name: Final Project
phases.focus: End-to-end delivery chain, presented to the group
phases.intro: Teams of two or three assemble everything from the programme into one working delivery chain for a provided application, then present it as they would to an engineering manager.

chapters.title: Brief & Design
chapters.content: Read the brief, draw the target architecture, split the work into a backlog

chapters.title: Build
chapters.content: Git workflow, CI pipeline with quality gate and artifacts, infrastructure with Terraform and Ansible, deployment to Kubernetes

chapters.title: Monitor & Document
chapters.content: Dashboards and alerts, README, architecture diagram, runbook

chapters.title: Demo & Review
chapters.content: Live demo of a change going from commit to production, questions, feedback

project.title: From Commit to Production
project.brief: A change pushed to Git is tested, analysed, versioned and deployed automatically to infrastructure that the team provisioned in code, and its health is visible on a dashboard with alerts.
project.stack: Git, GitHub, Jenkins or GitHub Actions, SonarQube, Nexus, Terraform, Ansible, Docker, Kubernetes, Prometheus, Grafana
project.deliverable: Repository with pipeline and infrastructure code, architecture diagram, runbook, live demo
